glyph_origin: Pictogram (象形) – a snake's tongue emerging upwards from a mouth (口). Evolution: • Oracle bone script: Originally a mouth + a forked snake tongue. Later variants added a horizontal stroke at the base to indicate location, which often evolved into a second fork (double-forked). • Bronze script (Late Shang / Early Western Zhou): Standardized with four dots symmetrically placed between the double forks and the mouth. • Later: The dots disappeared, simplifying into the modern form. Compare 舌 and 蛇 (“snake”). See also 言, 音 and 告. Unrelated to 舍, in which it represents a hut.
